terms.comment: Quintilian’s word, from appōnere, to set beside: the adjective as a kind of word, which some wanted always placed after its noun (9.4.24), and the epithet, Greek epitheton (8.6.40).

evidence: Prisc. p. 578 P. (Lewis & Short, s.v. adjectīvus)
M-O s.v. parts of speech: adjective
terms.comment: The grammarians’ nōmen adjectīvum, the noun ‘added’ to another (Priscian, Macrobius), and the term of every later grammar.

evidence: Quint. 8.6.40: ōrnat enim epitheton, quod rēctē dīcimus appositum
M-O s.v. parts of speech: adjective
terms.comment: The Greek word, of an adjective added for ornament.

terms.gloss: in grammar, the passive: modify, be added to (a noun)
terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation; passive with the dative
evidence: Traupman 346, 347: adjicior (+ dat.), modify; adjectus, modifying

phrases.latin: illa nimia quōrundam fuit observātiō, ut vocābula verbīs, verba rūrsus adverbiīs, nōmina appositīs et prōnōminibus essent priōra
phrases.english: Some were too scrupulous in insisting that nouns should come before verbs, verbs before adverbs, nouns before adjectives and pronouns

phrases.latin: ōrnat enim epitheton, quod rēctē dīcimus appositum
phrases.english: for the epithet, which we rightly call appositum, adds ornament
